records.name: Cerebellum
records.function: Processes input from the premotor cortex, brain stem and sensory receptors to provide feedback for precise, coordinated movements of skeletal muscles; plays a major role in balance (S8).
records.connections: Connected to the brain stem by three paired peduncles: inferior (to the medulla, conveying sensory/proprioceptive input), middle (the ventral pons, conveying a copy of cortical motor commands) and superior (to the midbrain and thalamus, its major output) (S8).
records.note: Comprises about 10-11% of brain mass and lies dorsal to the pons and medulla (S8). The release names no cerebellar nucleus, vermis or flocculus (probe-verified absences); the record's geometry is the whole-organ composition only.

records.name: Brainstem
records.function: Controls automatic behaviours necessary for survival and serves as a conduit for fibre tracts connecting higher and lower neural centres (S8). Cranial nerves III-XII arise from the brainstem (S1).
records.connections: Continuous cranially with the diencephalon and caudally, via the medulla, with the spinal cord at the foramen magnum (S8).
records.note: Consists of the midbrain, pons and medulla oblongata (S8). In the release the brainstem concept hangs in the PART-OF tree under head proper, not under the nervous system (see inventory).

records.name: Midbrain
records.function: Contains the corpora quadrigemina (superior and inferior colliculi), the visual and auditory reflex centres, and the cerebral aqueduct connecting the third and fourth ventricles (S8). Cranial nerves III and IV arise from it (S1).
verify: connections: not sourced from consulted sources - verify

records.name: Pons
records.function: Chiefly composed of conduction tracts between higher brain centres and the spinal cord, and of tracts connecting the pons to the cerebellum (S8). The trigeminal nerve (CN V) arises from it (S1).
records.connections: Relays cortical motor commands to the cerebellum via the middle cerebellar peduncle (S8).

records.name: Medulla oblongata
records.function: Contains the cardiovascular centre, which adjusts the force and rate of heart contraction and regulates blood vessel diameter (S8); controls vital involuntary functions including breathing, heart rate, blood pressure and digestion, and relays nerve signals between brain and body (S11). Cranial nerves IX-XII arise from it (S1).
verify: connections: not sourced from consulted sources - verify
records.note: Blends into the spinal cord at the foramen magnum (S8). The release's medulla record carries no named nuclei or olives (probe-verified absences).

ta_name: ambiguous in TA2 (FIPAT 2nd ed., version 2.07) consulted 2026-11-06 — TA2 lists 'basal ganglia' only as a related term of 5559 corpus striatum, whose structure differs from this record (corpus striatum = caudate + lentiform nuclei; the record covers the basal nuclei group); no TA2 preferred or synonym term denotes the basal ganglia.

records.name: Brain
records.parts: Cerebrum (two cerebral hemispheres, each with frontal, parietal, temporal and occipital lobes), cerebellum, brainstem (midbrain, pons, medulla oblongata) and diencephalon (thalamus, hypothalamus and associated structures).
records.function: The cerebral hemispheres localise and interpret sensory inputs, control voluntary and skilled skeletal muscle activity, and function in intellectual and emotional processing (S8); the remaining parts are covered by their own records.
verify: ventricular system: the release models the lateral, third and fourth ventricles and the cerebral aqueduct as concepts and records, but the choroid plexus exists only as the single class 'choroid plexus of cerebral hemisphere' and there is no ependyma or septum pellucidum concept — CSF production anatomy is therefore incomplete in v1 - verify
records.note: Geometry links the PART-OF brain organ record (its composition is the whole-brain mesh set). Cranial nerves I and II arise from the cerebrum and III-XII from the brainstem (S1).

records.name: Spinal cord
records.segments: 31 segments: 8 cervical, 12 thoracic, 5 lumbar, 5 sacral and 1 coccygeal, each giving origin to a pair of spinal nerves (S10). Each spinal nerve forms from an anterior (motor) and a posterior (sensory) root uniting at the intervertebral foramen, then divides into posterior and anterior rami (S9).
records.structure: Arises cranially as a continuation of the medulla oblongata and travels within the vertebral canal surrounded by the spinal meninges (dura mater, arachnoid mater, pia mater). At the L2 vertebral level it tapers to the conus medullaris; the spinal nerves arising beyond it form the cauda equina. Two enlargements: cervical (C4-T1, origin of the brachial plexus) and lumbar (T11-L1, origin of the lumbar and sacral plexi). Distally the meninges form the filum terminale, anchoring the cord to the coccyx (S9).
records.arterial_supply: Three longitudinal arteries: the anterior spinal artery (from the vertebral arteries) and the paired posterior spinal arteries (from the vertebral artery or the posteroinferior cerebellar artery), reinforced by anterior and posterior segmental medullary arteries; the largest, the artery of Adamkiewicz, supplies the inferior two thirds of the cord (S9).
